segments.text: A fish swims along, opening and closing its mouth.
But it's not drinking - it's breathing.
Water it takes in flows out through the gill slits.
Gills are thin tissue stacked in layers.
Tiny blood vessels run densely through it.
As water passes, oxygen slips into the blood.
Out of water, those layers stick together.
So they can't take in oxygen, and can't breathe.
